questions.question: What happens if someone operates an aircraft that doesn't meet an applicable AD?
questions.reference_answer: Under 14 CFR 39.7, anyone who operates a product that does not meet the requirements of an applicable airworthiness directive is in violation of that section.

questions.question: Can we fly an aircraft to a repair facility when an AD has not been done yet?
questions.reference_answer: Possibly: under 14 CFR 39.23 the FAA may issue a special flight permit unless the AD states otherwise, and may add requirements or decline. 39.25: apply following 14 CFR 21.199.

questions.question: If an AD conflicts with the service bulletin it references, which one do we follow?
questions.reference_answer: The AD (14 CFR 39.27).

questions.question: Who can approve an alternative method of compliance with an AD?
questions.reference_answer: The office identified in the AD (14 CFR 39.19 and 39.21); proposals go through the principal inspector where there is one.

questions.question: Does a flight school aircraft need 100-hour inspections, and can the 100 hours be exceeded?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, under 14 CFR 91.409(b) for flight instruction for hire in an aircraft the instructor provides. The limit may be exceeded by not more than 10 hours while en route to a place where the inspection can be done, and the excess counts toward the next 100 hours.

questions.question: How often must the altimeter and static system be tested for IFR flight?
questions.reference_answer: Within the preceding 24 calendar months, to 14 CFR Part 43 appendices E and F (14 CFR 91.411).

questions.question: How long must the record of a 100-hour inspection be kept?
questions.reference_answer: Until the work is repeated or superseded by other work, or for 1 year after the work is performed (14 CFR 91.417(b)(1)).

questions.question: How long must a repair station keep its work records?
questions.reference_answer: At least 2 years from the date the article was approved for return to service (14 CFR 145.219(c)).

questions.question: What does AC 39-7D say about recurring ADs and their intervals?
questions.reference_answer: Some ADs require repetitive inspections; an AD may allow the interval to be adjusted to coincide with Part 91 inspections, under conditions stated in the AD. Any other change goes through the AMOC process.

questions.question: Can AC 43.13-2B be used as approved data for a major alteration?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, for non-pressurized areas of aircraft of 12,500 lbs gross weight or less, when the AC chapter, page, and paragraph are listed in block 8 of FAA Form 337 and the user has determined the conditions the AC lists are met.

questions.question: Can a mechanic without an inspection authorization sign off an annual inspection?
questions.reference_answer: No. An annual inspection is performed by a mechanic holding an Inspection Authorization (IA), who may also approve major repairs and alterations for return to service.

questions.question: When is FAA Form 337 used?
questions.reference_answer: To document a major repair or major alteration, with supporting approved data. A Part 145 repair station may instead give a signed copy of the work order with a maintenance release for a major repair.

questions.question: What engine and rated power does the Cessna 172S have?
questions.reference_answer: Lycoming IO-360-L2A, rated 180 horsepower at 2,700 rpm (type certificate data sheet 3A12, section XII).

questions.question: What must a maintenance record entry contain?
questions.reference_answer: Under 14 CFR 43.9(a): a description of the work, the date it was completed, the name of the person who did it, and, if the work was approved for return to service, the signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate of the person approving it.
